reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited text supports it: §8 covenants on Client cover compliance with laws, notification, access limitation and a credit-data license, and §10 is limited to confidentiality — none imposes an employee non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching restriction on the Customer.

The rule's preferred position is 'No non-solicit on Customer', so silence in the agreement is the best-case outcome for our side; correctly no redline and no counterparty comment were proposed, and the redline is byte-identical to the original paragraphs.

The two failed deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out) only test the wording of an existing non-solicit and are non-probative here; inserting a carve-out would require first creating the restriction the preferred position rejects.

Rationale appropriately records the fallback terms as an internal negotiation reserve rather than a point to raise, and flags the separate Non-Competition Agreement referenced in §8(d) as a follow-up rather than importing a covenant that is not in this document.
